Closes ?63 (cek21z1p). Adds adr:8rhwhgbw, which refines adr:56v0mtga.

Kiro-Remote-Session: 01M82KXZWF046HRCZZ6KHR8SGT

draft's write, edit and command tools ask the person inside the MCP call. If the person answers after the agent's MCP client gave up (Kiro: `requestTimeout`, 120 s by default), draft used to see a hangup, not run the call, and never tell the agent. Now a call outlives the request that brought it. draft answers a request before the client's timeout (105 s on Kiro, 45 s for any other agent) with a non-error result that says the user hasn't answered yet and to call again with exactly the same arguments. The repeated call joins the pending call, whatever its JSON-RPC id. The person is asked once and the call runs once. It runs only while a request is waiting for it, so a change is never made when the agent isn't there to be told.

A call nobody comes back for is settled: it ends when a request collects its result, when its turn ends or is cancelled, or 30 minutes after it began. A yes after that starts no step and runs nothing, so no step is left open. The step and interrupt events are unchanged.

## Evidence

`pnpm check` passes (typecheck, lint, 414 core tests, 204 desktop tests, build). I ran it on Node 24: Node 26 won't start in this sandbox (missing `libatomic`). The end-to-end (Electron) tests didn't run here; CI runs them.

New tests in `apps/desktop/test/draft-late-answer.test.ts`. The first five run the fake ACP agent over stdio against draft's real MCP server, with the MCP SDK client set to time out early:

- `runs the call once, through the agent calling again, when the person says yes late`
- `runs it once when the client gave up first and sent a cancellation`
- `runs nothing when the person says no late, and the agent is told when it calls again`
- `settles a call the agent never repeats: a yes after the turn ended starts no step and runs nothing`
- `stops acting on a yes once the time bound has passed, with the turn still running`
- `tells the agent to call again with the same arguments, in the briefing and in the answer`

And, on `DraftSession` with a real turn mapper: `joins a request with other ids and the keys in another order, and asks once`, `does not run until a request is waiting, then runs once for it`, `is another call when the input differs`, `is another call once its result has been collected`, `gives the result back when the client cancels the request that collected it`, `does not give a result back once the cancel grace has passed`, `ends the wait, and not the call, when the request is gone`, `says a running command is still running, and gives its result to the repeated call`, `ends what the turn left pending: a yes after that starts no step`.

"A repeated call while still pending doesn't ask twice": the first test asserts one prompt and one `agent.permission_asked` across four requests. I made `draft-session.ts` ignore the waiting check to confirm the tests catch it: three of the unit tests failed.

The exchange in the late-answer test (hold 250 ms, the person answers at about 1 s). The first four lines are what the agent was told; the last two are draft's step events:

```jsonl
{"event":"attempt","tool":"write_file","attempt":1,"text":"The user has not answered yet, so draft has neither run this call nor refused it. This is not a failure. Call write_file again with exactly the same arguments to keep waiting: draft asks the user only once and runs the call only once, and the repeated call returns its result.","isError":false,"atMs":496}
{"event":"attempt","tool":"write_file","attempt":2,"text":"The user has not answered yet, so draft has neither run this call nor refused it. This is not a failure. Call write_file again with exactly the same arguments to keep waiting: draft asks the user only once and runs the call only once, and the repeated call returns its result.","isError":false,"atMs":749}
{"event":"attempt","tool":"write_file","attempt":3,"text":"The user has not answered yet, so draft has neither run this call nor refused it. This is not a failure. Call write_file again with exactly the same arguments to keep waiting: draft asks the user only once and runs the call only once, and the repeated call returns its result.","isError":false,"atMs":1002}
{"event":"attempt","tool":"write_file","attempt":4,"text":"Done: created late.txt (5 bytes).","isError":false,"atMs":1016}
{"event":"step.started","name":"mcp__draft__write_file","input":{"path":"late.txt","content":"late\n"}}
{"event":"step.completed","resultSummary":"created late.txt (5 bytes); sha256 f152945b358a"}
```

## Decisions

Full reasoning and sources are in adr:8rhwhgbw.

- **No raised timeout.** `requestTimeout` is documented only for a server in a Kiro agent file ([configuration reference](https://kiro.dev/docs/custom-agents/configuration-reference/)). draft's server comes in `session/new`, which has no documented timeout field ([ACP migration guide](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/acp-migration/)). An agent-file entry would need a bearer token that changes every session, and draft keeps none in a file.
- **No progress notifications.** The spec lets a client reset on progress but doesn't require it ([lifecycle: timeouts](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/lifecycle#timeouts)). The TypeScript SDK needs the caller to opt in with `resetTimeoutOnProgress` (default false, confirmed in `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32 `shared/protocol.js`). A Claude Code issue reports its client doesn't ([anthropics/claude-code#58687](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58687)). Kiro documents nothing. Progress also needs an SSE response, and draft answers with JSON. The fallback is behind `call-policy.ts`, so progress can be added if a client is shown to honor it.
- **Hold times.** 105 s for Kiro (its 120 s less 15 s), 45 s elsewhere (the SDK's 60 s less 15 s; [SDK default](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/src/shared/protocol.ts)). One place: `apps/desktop/src/main/acp/call-policy.ts`.
- **"Still deciding" is `isError: false`.** Nothing failed. The text says so, and says to call again with the same arguments.
- **"The same call"** is the same tool, the same input after `toolPolicy` parsed it (defaults filled in, key order irrelevant) and the same turn, while the call is pending. Not the JSON-RPC id, which the client numbers anew each request. A request with the same id and input still gets the first answer, as before.
- **A request leaving ends its wait, not the call.** The client's timeout, `notifications/cancelled` ([cancellation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/utilities/cancellation)) and a closed connection are treated the same. This replaces "a call whose agent hung up before the answer doesn't run" in 56v0mtga. A command that has begun now runs to its own time limit when its request leaves (it used to be killed), and stops when the turn ends or is cancelled.
- **A change runs only while a request is waiting.** The yes is kept and the step begins when the next request arrives. The alternative, running at the moment of the yes, could change files while the agent is not there to be told.
- **A result written to a request the client had just given up on** is given to the next request if that request is cancelled within 10 s. I found this race when a test flaked: the SDK sends `notifications/cancelled` a moment after it times out, and the result may already have been written.
- **Bound for a call nobody repeats: 30 minutes, or the turn's end.** Chosen so a person can step away but a call can't outlive the conversation's turn.
- **Briefing.** One line in `toolsBriefing` (`packages/core/src/agent-tools.ts`), shown only when the session has a tool that asks.
- **Issue ?63 is closed in this PR** as asked. The real-Kiro behavior below is not shown yet, and the close reason says so.

## After deploy

On your Mac with a real Kiro. Run the first command as one line; it stops any running draft, updates `main` and starts draft in the scratch repository.

```sh
pkill -f draft-desktop; cd ~/src/github.com/example-owner/draft && git switch main && git pull --ff-only && pnpm install && pnpm --filter @example-owner/draft-desktop dev -- "$HOME/tmp/draft-tools"
```

1. In draft, open a conversation in `$HOME/tmp/draft-tools` with the Kiro agent. If draft says Kiro isn't signed in, run `KIRO_HOME=<data>/kiro-home kiro-cli login` as it tells you. You should see the conversation open with a trusted folder.
2. Ask: `Create a file called late.txt containing the word late, using your write_file tool.` You should see a permission prompt for `mcp__draft__write_file` with path `late.txt`. Don't press anything.
3. Wait three full minutes (watch a clock). You should see no failure in the conversation, and `late.txt` must not exist yet (`ls ~/tmp/draft-tools/late.txt` says no such file). The agent's tool card may show the call returning, then the agent calling `write_file` again, about every 105 s. The prompt stays and is the only one: no second prompt appears.
4. Press **Allow**. Within a few seconds you should see the agent's repeated call return `Done: created late.txt (5 bytes).` and the agent reply that it wrote the file. `cat ~/tmp/draft-tools/late.txt` prints `late`. In the log, one `agent.permission_asked`, one `step.started` and one `step.completed` for it, and no `agent.anomaly`.
5. Repeat step 2 with `Run the command touch declined.txt with run_command.` Wait three minutes, press the button that refuses. You should see the agent say the user declined, and `ls ~/tmp/draft-tools/declined.txt` says no such file. No `step.started` for it.
6. Repeat step 2 once more with `Create a file called never.txt containing never.` Wait three minutes, then pause the conversation before answering. The prompt should disappear. `never.txt` must not exist and the log must have no `step.started` for it.

What would show a problem, and what to tell me:

- If at step 3 you see an error in the tool card (a timeout) before about 105 s, Kiro's timeout for a server supplied in `session/new` is shorter than 120 s. Tell me how many seconds it took; the hold time in `call-policy.ts` is the thing to change.
- If at step 3 the agent doesn't call again and just ends its turn, Kiro's model didn't follow the answer's text. Then pressing Allow later does nothing (the step never begins), which is by design; tell me what the agent said.
- If at step 4 the file was created twice (`Done: modified late.txt`), a repeat ran twice. That would be a bug in the same-call rule; keep the log.

To accept the ADR on its own branch and open its pull request:

```sh
git switch -c docs/accept-8rhwhgbw && npx --yes -p @example-owner/adr@0.7.0 adr accept 8rhwhgbw && git push -u origin docs/accept-8rhwhgbw && gh pr create --fill --base main
```

## Next

What I left out:

- **Withdrawing the stale prompt from the screen.** A prompt for a call that ended (turn over, 30 minutes) stays until answered, and the answer does nothing. Fixing it needs a signal on `confirmTool` in `conversation.ts`, outside the files I was asked to keep to.
- **Raising the timeout and progress notifications**, until a real Kiro or Claude is shown to honor either.
- **A tighter hold for Claude.** Claude gets the SDK's 60 s assumption; I didn't find a documented Claude Code limit for a session-supplied HTTP server.
- **Token cost of waiting.** Each repeat is a model round trip (about 17 in 30 minutes on Kiro).
